runbooks.diagnosis: calrs 1.6.0's dashboard event-type editor stores the literal title as location_value — so a seeded 'call' row got 'Discovery Call' instead of the VC room template, breaking booking links. calrs v1.6.0's CLI has no location flags, so fixing it requires a direct sqlite helper. DB: volume compose_calrs-data, /var/lib/calrs/calrs.db, owner calrs:calrs (999:999), WAL mode.
remediation: Stop opensme-calendar (never touch the DB writable while the app is up — WAL)
One-shot helper: sudo docker run --rm -i -v compose_calrs-data:/data alpine:3.19 sh -c 'apk add --no-cache sqlite >/dev/null 2>&1 && sqlite3 /data/calrs.db'
UPDATE event_types SET location_value='https://vc.<domain>/room/{uid}' WHERE slug='call'; plus a guarded INSERT (where not exists) for a new 'chat' type
Start calendar, then docker restart opensme-calendar-radicale (passenger re-attach)

runbooks.diagnosis: Only the admin 'demo' account owns event types; 'testuser' (the OIDC operator account) has none — so /u/testuser/vc returns 'Event type not found' while /u/demo/vc works. Event types are per-account.
remediation: Book and verify against the account that owns the event-type slug
When a user reports 'Event type not found', check which account owns the slug and their event type exists
Copy or recreate the event type on the target account if needed

runbooks.diagnosis: calrs sync reports ZERO calendars when its PROPFIND/resourcetype probe doesn't match Radicale's serialization (see radicale runbook: <C:calendar /> with uppercase prefix and space). The sync then thinks no collection exists.
remediation: Probe for the collection with PROPFIND 207 and check the resourcetype tag presence
Match the spaced/uppercase <C:calendar /> form rather than an exact lowercase string
Cross-reference the radicale resourcetype-probe runbook for the exact quirk
